statement_summary: Security lead and Affirming Official designated in writing
Annual risk assessment with supply chain threats
Risk acceptance authority; High risks never accepted
Sanctions recorded; good-faith reporting protected
No SPRS entry, affirmation, or SAM representation without documented support
Annual Level 1 self-assessment and independent control assessment
Vendor approval before FCI; annual MSP evidence
Sourcing order: authorized sources first; brokers only after approval
Section 889 screening of SKUs and company-owned equipment
Supplier purchase order flowdown and notice terms
Bank-detail changes verified by call-back; first payment held
Six-year retention of security and assessment records
Annual policy review; time-limited exceptions; none for FAR 52.204-21
Unique accounts including supplier portals and carrier
Least privilege; FCI folder for 4 named staff; 2 ERP administrators
MFA everywhere including MSP-held administrator logins
Termination checklist completed by the last day
Monthly account reconciliation and log review
10-minute lock on every computer
Named MSP and vendor accounts with MFA
Password rules; no password files; individual alarm codes
Door closed; visitors signed in and escorted; logs kept 1 year; key log
Setup bench on its own segment, named accounts, encrypted, company USB only
Open FCI only when the job needs it
No FCI in personal email, cloud, messaging, or public AI
Lock screens; never share passwords or MFA codes
Training at hire and yearly; phishing simulations
Report suspected incidents and suspect products at once
Signed policy acknowledgment
Nothing about DoD customers posted publicly
Supplier compromise runbook kept and printed
Report suspected incidents and suspect products within 1 hour
Log every incident with discovery and identification times
Stop-ship and quarantine suspect items until disposition
Government reports on time (889: 1 business day; Kaspersky: 3 business days; 252.246-7008 notice)
Insurer hotline first; MSP engaged under contract
Extortion payment only with approvals and OFAC check
Personal information notices under Fla. Stat. 501.171 and other states
Supplier and vendor incident notices logged and handled
Annual tabletop exercise with the MSP
Lessons learned within 30 days
Three classification levels
Encrypt Restricted data at rest and in transit
Restricted data only in approved systems; bench holds active job only
No CUI accepted; refuse and escalate
Device and data inventory with manufacturer of record
New tools and vendors approved before Restricted data
1-year immutable backup versions; quarterly restore test
Wipe or certified destruction with a disposal log
Approved AI tools only; no FCI in any AI tool
No DoD customer details on public sites; Owner approves posts
Retention of security records
